responses.text: I buy that.
Why does everyone always say that?

topics.prompt: It's time for us to part ways.

responses.text: What is this, the Hokey Pokey?

topics.prompt: On second thought, stick with me for a little longer.

responses.text: Okay. Then I guess I'll be back at the 188. Maybe digging in some dirt for scrap metal or something. {Guilting.}

topics.prompt: I just think we should right now.
topics.label: Yes, I'm sure.

responses.text: Nice! Can I order room service?

topics.prompt: I do. We'll meet up at the Lucky 38.
topics.label: I'd like you to go back to the Lucky 38 for now.

responses.text: Let's go make trouble.
Ooo. Sorry. Don't want to be a third wheel, you know?

topics.prompt: I think we should travel together.

responses.text: Aw, just when the standing around was getting exciting. {playful, not derisive.}
Hey, I can't really move, now. But I'll follow you in spirit.
Am I punching too much? I get carried away.
My recommendation - more punching.

topics.prompt: I want you to change your combat style.

responses.text: You mean like, even more?
Beats waiting till they shoot me first.

topics.prompt: I want you to attack enemies the moment you see them.

responses.text: Yeah. Shake things up a little.
Count me in.
You mean like this melee weapon right here in my hand at this very second?
Yes! Finally. Everything's coming up Veronica.
I like this plan where you're the decoy.
What a coincidence! I've been doing that all this time! {cheerily sarcastic}

topics.prompt: I want you not to attack enemies unless I've already engaged them.

responses.text: {Hopeful} Does jumping at them with my fists count as ranged? {Then, dejected} <Sighs> Fine.
Are you talking to me, or a future Veronica who is not already doing that?

topics.prompt: I want you to use ranged weapons.

responses.text: What are you saying, exactly? {As though being broken up with, but lightly}

topics.prompt: Let's talk about how close you're following me.

responses.text: Hey, now. You're gonna have to buy me dinner first.
This is as close as I get until you turn into a leggy brunette.
Sorry. I get distracted. Been scavenging too long.
See? I'm good at stuff.

topics.prompt: Your distance is good. Let's talk about something else.

responses.text: Good talk.

topics.prompt: All right, you're good. Let's get out of here.

responses.text: They'll never see the haymakers coming.

topics.label: Keep your distance. Try to flank them.

responses.text: Yeah. Screw them. {Cheerily jumping on the bandwagon.}
Ooo. Got something good for me? Is it a dress?
You're making me carry the heavy stuff, aren't you? {Accusatory}
Shoulda brought something to read...
Leave me alone.
Hey, you got a second?
I'd slap him around, but he stood at my parents' wedding.
Plus he used to make excuses to get me out of my punishment when I'd slept through Head Scribe Taggart's lectures. Figure I owe him for that.
<Sighs> He means well.
I'd be angrier with him, but it's hard to stay mad at the guy who taught me how to box when all the other Paladins told me no.
<Sighs> He always does what he feels is right. Usually that's a great quality.
Let's see what we've got here... Okay, yeah, this is the one I was thinking of. The pulse gun.
Although maybe the rangefinder could work too. And it looks like the NCR was onto some miracle farming technology.
{Defeated} He wouldn't listen. The truth was right there staring him in the face. How could he not listen?
{Disbelieving} God. {Then, saddened} I should get used to this, I guess. People get desperate, they turn on each other. First thing to go is trust.
I don't think it's ever gonna be the same for me in there. Knowing no matter what I do, it's gonna end badly.
But they're all I have. {Shaking her head, lost.}
{Remorseful} God, I did this. This was my fault. Why didn't I see this coming?
Of course they'd track me. Of course they'd assume the worst. Sure, I left them. But that didn't mean I'd ever be free of them.
I should've known I was beaten before I began. I just... I had to try, you know?
Well, if there was any question whether I should leave, I guess there's my answer.
{Horrified} Why did you do that? They were going to let us walk away. Why did you attack them?
I don't care that they started it. What you did was inexcusable. You need to go.
Clearly you're determined to fight the Brotherhood. Well, you can add my name to your hit list because you're on your own.
Okay, listen. The Brotherhood... they're not always the friendliest bunch. But I won't stand for you fighting them.
This is your last chance.
See? Pretty addictive, right? You do it once, it just makes you want to do it more.
You can't help but notice that the Brotherhood barely exists to these people out here. We're like an urban myth. No real presence on the Outside.
We just don't adapt like we should. Used to be that all you needed to get your way was a suit of power armor and a laser rifle.
Now... people are armed and organized. They're not afraid. But we still stick to our old approach, because it's all we know.
You know, I've been thinking. The real problem with the Brotherhood is that we isolate ourselves.
Our training is top-notch, our technology gives us an advantage, but when it all comes down to it, we're losing because we shun the outside world.
We always make enemies, never allies. We refuse to recruit outsiders, or see the value in their simpler technologies.
Hold on. I see something I want to punch.
No offense, but you look like you've traveled a long way down some bad roads. Where'd you come from?
Couldn't get enough of talking to me the first time, huh?
Listen... I want to thank you for helping me out. I'm sorry that... things didn't go like I'd hoped. {Beside herself}
But at least I got the chance to try. At least I know for sure that there was nothing I could do.
Thank you for giving me that chance.
Wow, Mr. House is looking for you, huh? What do you think he wants? Bowling partner?
What'd you think of Mr. House? I was surprised he only had the two robot sex slaves.
That chip of yours... I wouldn't wager it on blackjack.
Unless the dealer has a five or six showing.
Whole future of New Vegas seems like it's up in the air. Guess I should wait things out before buying a condo in the Ultra-Luxe, huh?
Hope you're picking the winning side here. Be nice to fight for someone who's gonna be around for a while.
Next stop, Hoover Dam, huh? When we get there... can we stop by the souvenir shop? Their beaver mascot is just precious.
What's up?
Am I gonna have to take that away from you?
Why do we always hurt the ones we care about the most? {wry}
Careful. Someone could trip on that. {calmly}
Grenade!
Oh god. He... {sighs} I guess he was lost a long time ago. Even at the end...
Still... thanks for bringing word. At least, now I know.

topics.prompt: Just mad ramblings. He didn't make much sense. (without Dead Money: Abraham wanted to say goodbye, and that he's gone North, into ghoul country.)

responses.text: {Drifting, dismissive} Hmm. Unlikely. He was a little too focused on gears and diodes... tech was the cure-all.

topics.prompt: He explained the search for the Sierra Madre... healed him. (without Dead Money: Abe explained what happened in the Crater, how it healed him.)

responses.text: Would you mind if I looked at the message?
Would you mind if I listened to the message?
Would you mind if I looked at the message you found?
Would you mind if I listened to the message you found?
{Irritated} Fine. I guess it doesn't matter anyway, keep it. I won't ask again.

topics.prompt: It's better you don't. Let me hold onto it. (without Dead Money: VDialogueVeronicaAbeMsgRefuse)

responses.text: {Waiting for player to step out of simulator} What was on it? What did he say?

topics.prompt: Some last words - a message. Nothing important. (without Dead Money: VDialogueVeronicaAbeSim1)

responses.text: {Sadly accepting} Yeah. Yeah. Thought as much. He'd been fading away for a long time.

topics.prompt: Can you unlock it for me first? He was... vague on that point. (without Dead Money: What did you expect a ghoul to say?)

responses.text: {Surprise, player found someone she thought was dead} You did? Where? Oh my God, I mean... I thought... I don't even know what I thought might have happened to him.
{Wary} But... you don't have a "this is good news" expression on your face.

topics.prompt: I found Elijah. (without Dead Money: I found the ghoul with the Accelerator you were looking for.)

responses.text: {Default Choke Node} ...it doesn't matter. He died when we all retreated to Hidden Valley. I didn't expect to see him again, no one did.
You killed him? {Beat} But...

topics.prompt: I had to kill him. (without Dead Money: I had to kill Monte for it.)

responses.text: Did he say anything when you met him? Anything...{about me, stops herself} anything at all?
Where did you get this?
{Wary} Guess I was right about the bad news, huh? Same look Elder McNamara always gave me when I was up for promotion.

topics.prompt: He left this holo-message. Here. (without Dead Money: Here's the accelerator.)

responses.text: {Given a farewell message} All right, I'll listen to it.

topics.prompt: You should listen to this. (without Dead Money: You should watch this.)

responses.text: {Given a farewell message} All right, I'll watch it.

topics.prompt: You should watch it. (without Dead Money: VDialogueVeronicaAcceleratorStg32)

responses.text: {Watched a goodbye message, slightly choked up} That was... that was hard to watch.
{Confused, a little disoriented} The parts I understood? Didn't matter. Past all the garbage, all it amounted to was goodbye.

topics.prompt: What did he say to you? (without Dead Money: What did Abraham say to you?)

responses.text: {Still a little dizzy} Sorry... feel a little out of it. Head's spinning a bit...
{Surprise, knowledge downloading} Oh. Oh!
{Blinking, just gained downloaded defense programs} I think he left me a gift. {Quiet} Maybe I can use it better than he did.
Trapped him? Where?

topics.prompt: I had to trap him inside a Pre-War... prison. (without Dead Money: I trapped Monte in a subway tunnel, that ghoul's not coming back.)

responses.text: {Trapped only} And I don't like saying this, but the Mojave's safer with him... there.
Step into my office.

topics.prompt: Could you help me craft something?

responses.text: Not sure what my parents would think of me fighting for the NCR.
But for New Vegas it seemed like this was the best chance at stability. I don't regret it.
Never sided with a group of marauders before. But I think the Brotherhood stands a better chance against them than they did against the NCR.
That gives me some hope.
For some reason, it warms my heart that we fought for the kooky old geezer. Guess he reminds me of someone.
Independent New Vegas. If that isn't redundant, I don't know what is.
But I like its chances.
Hey. I, uh, I can't go in with you. I'll wait here, okay?
<Gasps> For me? Do you mean it? No, no, it's too much! Well, okay. But it's too much! It's perfect. Thank you. Thank you.
I... wish I had something to give you. I- wait! What about punching? That's the gift that keeps on giving.
I could work on your punching with you, if you like. Show you how to counter like a Scribe.
Wow, you {emph} have come a long way, then. I've never been there, but I've met some traders who pass that way.
Well, welcome, then. I'm Veronica. I live in a hole in the ground.
Huh. Well, in that case I take it back. You look pretty good, given the circumstances.
Yeah, guess the roads must've been long, then, if you forgot where you started from.
That's why I asked. My business is boring. You try trading and scavenging for a living and see if you don't start nosing into other people's affairs.
Well, a bunker, if you want to get technical. I think it sounds more interesting my way.
But I'm not there much anymore. I'm usually out here picking up food and supplies for my family. Whatever they need.

topics.prompt: You live in a hole in the ground?

responses.text: Yeah. I'm not worried. They can handle themselves. But somebody has to get the groceries, know what I mean?
And actually these days I think they'd rather have me out here anyway. But that's a whole other story.
So, listen, can I ask you something on the level?

topics.prompt: So you just leave your family in the bunker?

responses.text: I had a run-in with this group calling themselves the Brotherhood of Steel. Pretty strange bunch. Do you know anything about them?
Forget I said anything, then.
Sure. It's a small wasteland. I'm sure we'll run into each other again.
And?

topics.prompt: I met a group of them in a bunker west of here.

responses.text: Well that shouldn't be a problem for me. I can't afford anything like that.

topics.prompt: They're usually harmless unless you use advanced technology around them.

responses.text: Oh my gosh, really? Well, I didn't see where they went, but I'll keep an eye out. Wow, I had no idea they were so dangerous.
Thanks for letting me know. Glad I didn't do any business with them.

topics.prompt: They're enemies of the NCR. If you know where they are you should turn them in.

responses.text: Do they? That's a relief. I wasn't so sure, myself. Protecting people from technology seems like a big job for such a small group.
Yeah, it's pretty far out, right? Fixating on old technology just doesn't seem very relevant to most people's lives.

topics.prompt: I know who they are but I don't care about their agenda.

responses.text: That bad, huh? Guess I'm lucky I got away with my life. I'll make sure and avoid them from now on. Thanks.

topics.prompt: Yeah. I know to shoot them on sight.

responses.text: That's okay, I wouldn't expect anybody to. I think they tend to keep to themselves.
God, you're not lying, are you? You really did kill them. {Horrifying realization.}
In that case, this is for them. {Spiteful.}
You think? Well good, then. That puts me a little more at ease.
Hey, so where are you headed, anyway?
That seems wise. I think I am, too. Although for how much longer, I'm not sure.
Not very friendly, are they?
Well, thanks for weighing in. Gives me something to think about.
Wow. I've got to admit, you have completely defied my first impression of you. {amused at idiocy}
Eye lasers. I'll be sure and look out for that next time.
Any other juicy bits of intel?

topics.prompt: I've heard they shoot lasers from their eyes.

responses.text: Ooo. Very exciting. Gonna strike it rich, huh?
Huh. Just on your way to do a little heavily fortified sightseeing. Kind of a thrillseeker, aren't you?
Just wherever the wind takes you, huh? I like that. Keeps things interesting.

topics.prompt: I just kind of drift from place to place.

responses.text: I'll be honest. You're the first person I've run across out here that looks like he can really handle himself.
I'll be honest. You're the first person I've run across out here that looks like she can really handle herself.
There are places I've never been to that'd be too dangerous for just me. What do you think? Maybe we could travel together, help each other out.
Guess we have that in common, then.
This is quite a journey you're going on, then. Must be an interesting relationship to have brought you all this way.

topics.prompt: Going to see an old friend.

responses.text: Heh. Good. That's the look I was going for. Trust me on this one, though. You'll be glad you brought me along.
If I turn out to be a burden, we can part ways at any time. No hard feelings.

topics.prompt: You don't look like much. What do you bring to the table?

responses.text: Oh, nowhere in particular, really. Just hoping to see more of the world. Looking for a fresh perspective.
I want to see how different groups have adapted to survive in the Mojave. See if there's something I can learn from.

topics.prompt: Where are you hoping to go?

responses.text: Now you're talking. One thing you should know, first, though. I asked you about the Brotherhood because I'm one of them.
I know, I know. But I had to know how you'd react when I told you. We've made a lot of enemies.
You still okay bringing me along?
Aw, you really know how to make a girl feel like a stray cat.
But okay. My offer stands, if we run into each other again.

topics.prompt: I'd like to, but I can't take you with me right now.

responses.text: Suit yourself. You can always change your mind.
Like I said, they can handle themselves. And I'm not the only one getting supplies for them. It's a big family.

topics.prompt: Don't you have a family to feed?

responses.text: Good. I hoped you'd come around. Shall we?

topics.prompt: I'm ready to travel with you.

responses.text: I'm great at punching people. I'm not gonna lie. It's a gift.
Well, thanks for taking a chance on a naive young girl from California with stars in her eyes and a pneumatic gauntlet on her hand.
Let's hit the road, huh?

topics.prompt: Actually, I'm more comfortable now that I know you've had some training.

responses.text: Sure. Just don't ever ask me if your outfit makes you look fat.

topics.prompt: As long as you're honest with me from now on.

responses.text: Fair enough. Maybe one day I'll have your complete trust, and I can be on a long leash. A girl can dream.

topics.prompt: Yes, but you're on a short leash.

responses.text: The Brotherhood is failing. {Beat} I've always known that. If we don't change course, we're going to fall apart or... fade away.
But until recently I haven't understood where we went wrong, or how to fix it.
I think I need to go home.
I like long walks in the desert and candle-lit metal workshops.
My favorite subject.
He was dead when I got there.
This better not be about the meaning of life.
Well, when two people really love each other... you really don't know this stuff yet?
Ooo, do I get a prize if I answer right?
I was told we wouldn't be tested on this.
A lifetime supply of Fancy Lads Snack Cakes, revenge against my enemies, and world peace. In that order.
{Defensive} I was young and I needed the money.
It's a free wasteland.

topics.prompt: I have questions I wanted to ask you.

responses.text: Yeah. They say he built the Strip. Of course, they say a lot of things. No one's actually met him.
Me? I think it's a hoax. Probably a group of people who want to avoid attention, or some made-up persona of a self-aware computer.
Why else would he shut himself in like that?

topics.prompt: Ever heard of Mr. House before?

responses.text: Yeah. It's not for poker.
I've never seen anything quite like it, but I can tell you it looks like it was fabricated before the War, and not at a mint.
Some kind of tech... I'm gonna say... mid-2200s. Hold onto it. Might be your lucky chip.

topics.prompt: Can you tell me anything about this platinum chip?

responses.text: Sure, he's one of the hotel managers on the Strip. He comes up in the news now and then.
Him and the other Chairmen run the Tops. It's one of the nicer hotels, or so I hear.
Elder McNamara wouldn't shell out for a passport for me, so I've actually never been to the Strip. Why do people get so cheap when they get old?

topics.prompt: Ever hear of a guy called Benny?

responses.text: Yep. It's your typical city layout. Rich people in a gated community surrounded by extreme poverty.
House gave the area around the Strip to the locals, but he has no interest in it, so he ignores it entirely. It just needs new management.
I'd love to see the Brotherhood do it, but since the Codex doesn't say "clean up Freeside" no one listens to me. Bunch of sticklers.
I'm worried they'll be the death of the Brotherhood. They take what they want. We defend our interests to the death.
But there's a handful of us and tens or hundreds of thousands of them. So it's not going to end well.
Last time we clashed we lost a lot of people. Retreated to our bunker. Now we're afraid to even move around during the day.

topics.prompt: What do you think of the NCR?

responses.text: Silliest dressed band of raping, slaving marauders you'll see east of California, I'll say that. Where's that touch of Old World class?
Although I hear the soldiers mount each other as much as they mount their women, so maybe they did keep a little something from the Empire.
No such privilege for the women, though. Figures. So... to answer your question... they're a bunch of hypocritical jerkwads. {beat} It's a word.
Darn it, I had some spectacular answers coming, too.
Let's. {Pleasantly}
Okay. Well, when you do, let me know, all right?
Great. Thanks. Thank you. I'll encourage people to name their non-ugly children after you. Seriously.

topics.prompt: I'll take you back there, first chance I get.

responses.text: Sure, yeah. Just not too long, okay? I worry about them sometimes. {Not the ideal answer she wanted, but going with it, trying to stay upbeat.}
Wow, don't everybody volunteer all at once now.
I {emph} could do that. You're not interested in coming along? Hate to break up the band over a silly little thing like the future of everyone I care about.

topics.prompt: Why don't you just go back on your own?

responses.text: This from the girl who walked from I-15 to the Colorado River looking for her lost package.
This from the guy who walked from I-15 to the Colorado River looking for his lost package.
I hope you change your mind. {miffed}

topics.prompt: That's just not important right now.

responses.text: Not much for family gatherings, huh? All right, have it your way.
You ever want to look me up again, I'll be in my bunker in Hidden Valley. That's the {emph} luxury bunker.

topics.prompt: I have things I need to do. You'd better go alone.

responses.text: I'm not giving up. He wants evidence, but he'll never go looking for it. He's scared I'm right.
He'll never listen unless I hold the proof right in front of his face.
He's a stubborn old man, but when it comes down to it, he's got our best interests at heart.
If he sees some indisputable sign we're on the wrong course, he won't ignore it.

topics.prompt: You think the Elder will listen at all?

responses.text: I don't know. I don't know. We'd need something that shows the Brotherhood will fail. Or that it can do better a different way.
The only thing that'd get his attention is technology.
Huh. Maybe Father Elijah had the right idea.

topics.prompt: What could we bring to him that would change his mind?

responses.text: That's my question to the Elder. All these years, the Brotherhood has collected weapons technology. And for what?
To keep it out of people's hands? That clearly hasn't worked. To defend ourselves? We can't compete with the NCR's numbers. Or the Legion's.
We're fighting a war for a lost cause. If we're going to survive, we have to find a role in society. Attract new members.

topics.prompt: So what is it you're trying to accomplish?

responses.text: Look at the Followers of the Apocalypse. They use their expertise to improve people's lives. They train them to be self-sufficient.
That expertise cultivates respect and gratitude. Spreads their ideals. Draws talent to their cause. They make friends like we make enemies.
But they don't know a fraction of what we know. If we took on their role, we could stand up to anyone. We wouldn't have to hide.

topics.prompt: How would you propose to do that?

responses.text: Our Elder before McNamara. He had a nose for recovering lost technology. He'd send Scribes out into the desert chasing whatever leads he found.
There were a few he only trusted me with. I can think of at least one that'd prove my point, if it still exists.
There's a comm terminal not too far from here I'd use to access messages from him. If we go there I can pull up his research on it.
It's a targeting device for some kind of doomsday weapon based at HELIOS One. It was lost sometime after the War.
We held HELIOS One for a time. Lost a lot of people defending it. Too many. All for this weapon they never got working.
If it turns out to be a dud, it'd show how flawed our goals have been. Father Elijah said he thinks a scavenger might have sold it on the Strip.
I'm with you. Being around here isn't the same anymore.
No, but it does make it easier to forgive him. He's just misguided.
It's not too late to change his mind.

topics.prompt: Good intentions don't justify marching the Brotherhood to its death.

responses.text: Have {emph} you considered that he might be senile?
The Brotherhood's strategy for survival worked back when we had a larger force, and no organized enemies.
We're a tiny splinter from a shrinking group. We don't take on new members. But we're still picking fights with the big boys.

topics.prompt: Have you considered that he might be right?

responses.text: Electromagnetic weapon from before the Great War. Experimental. It never saw mass production.
But they were building it as a countermeasure to power armor, which they feared the Chinese were developing.
Supposedly a prototype was being housed at Nellis. Imagine what it could do to the Brotherhood. We'd be on equal footing with any idiot with a gun.
More or less. Supposedly it's a vegetation enhancer. NCR has a science branch headquartered at McCarran airport. Guess they found something.
Guess somebody wasn't very good at keeping secrets, either.
We'd never pursue it because it's not a weapon. But self-sufficiency is fundamental to us. If it works they'd see the value of an alternate course.
Yeah, maybe they'll think twice about engaging the NCR if they know one of those could be floating around.
The notes say to look around Nellis Air Force Base. He suggests going through filing cabinets and computers in the commanding officer's quarters.
They defended HELIOS like it was their last stand. Didn't even know if there was anything worth defending. How could there be, with all we lost?
Even if it did work, it'd be under NCR control now. So it'd either prove our goals are wrong or we're incapable of pursuing them.
There's a pawn shop in Outer Vegas we could check. And I've heard of a gift shop in the Strip that deals in Pre-War antiques.
Okay. What better way to persuade them than to give them a taste of what they stand to gain, right?
Maybe the best place to start is to see what we can find out directly from the NCR. Let's head to their OSI office at McCarran.

topics.prompt: We should go after the vegetation technology.

responses.text: I like the way you think.
I see that now. I thought I knew him better than that. But it was like talking to a stranger.

topics.prompt: There was never any chance. His mind was made up from the start.

responses.text: No. Our case wouldn't be any stronger if tomorrow they all died when their energy weapons backfired.
I just didn't expect that. There was no getting through to him.

topics.prompt: Maybe if we make a stronger case, he'll change his mind.

responses.text: Well I {emph} knew he wouldn't listen to {slight emph} me. That's why we went out of our way to find something that he couldn't ignore.
But it didn't make any difference.
How can I help them when they won't accept it?
Ah, hell. Well, how could you know, right? Okay. Two other options still on the table.

topics.prompt: The rangefinder might be a problem. I reactivated HELIOS One, and it's not powering a weapon.

responses.text: It pays like ass, but it's hard to get other work with my skill set.
What do you want to know?

topics.prompt: Tell me about the Brotherhood of Steel.

responses.text: It wouldn't matter. The Elder has final say.
The hell of it is he's one of our most progressive members. If I can't get him to agree, it's hopeless.
He won't tolerate any resistance. If he catches wind I've been talking to people, he'll charge me with sedition.

topics.prompt: Would someone else listen to you?

responses.text: I... {beat} I don't know if I can stay. Maybe it'd be better for everyone if I left. Spent my life... somewhere else. {This'd be a big deal for her. First sentence is a revelation.}
Work with the Followers of the Apocalypse, maybe. Put my knowledge to some good use. {Offhand, Not with a lot of hope}
Or I can stay here with the people I care about and do... whatever I can, until it comes to a slow or sudden end.
Ha! Well that's... imaginative. But it's not really for me.
I couldn't get one of their most reasonable members to accept a rational argument. I don't see them coming out in droves to support my coup.
And that's really not what the Brotherhood needs right now anyway. They're hanging by a thread.
Ha! Good question. These days it's hard to say. Once upon a time it was about technology. Controlling it so it couldn't destroy us again.
Energy weapons and power armor are usually tops on our list, although {emph} I appreciate anything that's vintage.
But that all seems so limited now. We haven't grown or adapted. And now we're stuck in a hole, not carrying out our mission.
They may be a bunch of wooden conformists, but anything I did without them would feel... empty.
I'd always be reminded of this day. How I wasn't strong enough to stand by them.
So I guess I'll stay. Won't be easy, but at least I won't feel guilty about the choice.
Let's get going. I'd like to get my mind off all this. And some fresh air would do me some good right about now.

topics.prompt: This is your home, and these are your friends. You should stay.

responses.text: There's no getting around that, is there? What would my life be like here, knowing what's to come?
They're not going to like this. We're given a chance when we're young to choose whether to stay. If we do, it's supposed to be for life.
But they haven't left me any choice. It's this or a lifetime of scavenging and watching my friends die in losing battles. {beat} I guess it's settled, then.

topics.prompt: Leaving now is your only shot at a future.

responses.text: Not even a hint, huh? Geez, I really am all alone on this one. {Sad.}
I guess I'll stay. If I left there wouldn't be any coming back. It might be something I'd instantly regret.
Things are going to get harder for the Brotherhood before they get easier. I should support them in whatever way I can.

topics.prompt: You're the only one who can make this decision.

responses.text: More sexual favors than I can even count. I am still tired from it.
No, actually, you're born into it. My parents, their parents, so on. When you're young you can choose to leave. But it's home, so most people don't.
We don't take on new members, really. You can do the math on our long-term prospects based on that point. I keep hoping we'll change that.

topics.prompt: How did you get to be a member?

responses.text: I'm a procurement specialist. Like I said, it's basically grocery shopping. Except sometimes the groceries are scavenged parts and arcane technology.
The elder who brought us to the Mojave, Father Elijah, usually had me looking for these old memory units. But he'd never tell me what they were for.
Nowadays I'm usually sent to do business with traders at places like the 188. But sometimes I think it's just to keep me out of everyone's hair.

topics.prompt: What do you do for them?

responses.text: I know sometimes I sound like I don't. I know. But there's something that still rings true to me about our code.
There's an honor to it. We're protecting people. Even if it's from themselves, it's a good cause.
We just lose sight of the big picture sometimes. Treat all our practices with the same sacredness.

topics.prompt: Do you like being a member?

responses.text: Ah, the Codex. If it's in there, we have to abide it, if it's not, it's not important. {She has a love-hate relationship with the Codex.}
It documents our history, too. Part of what Scribes like me do is update it. Hmm... I wonder...
Nah, they'd probably catch it if I rewrote the Founder's axioms.
No, no. We only protect people from {emph} themselves, and only in the sense that we don't let them have the really good Pre-War toys.
And sometimes it's more like we protect {emph} ourselves from {emph} them and hope to outlive them and become humanity's sole heirs.
We've had people go rogue, though, and start helping people. One chapter had a small civil war over it. We take our isolationism seriously.

topics.prompt: Does the Brotherhood protect people from raiders or other threats?

responses.text: I called them family before. That's not far off. Both the good and the bad. It's like a big unending family reunion in that bunker.
There's people you love, people you'll never speak to again, and it's always awkward when you run into someone you used to date.

topics.prompt: How do you feel about the other members?

responses.text: He was our Elder when we came East. A wizard with technology, really. His mind just worked that way naturally. Learned a lot from him.
But he started having disagreements with the other Elders. The Brotherhood's interest is in old technology. He wanted to explore developing new tech.
And there were other ways he wanted to push. Other weapons. Ones with ethics questions attached. Rather than deal with him, they sent him East.
I like punching things, but sometimes shooting things just has to do.

topics.prompt: How can I best use your skills?

responses.text: {"Go ahead and ask."} Shoot.
What are your thoughts?

topics.prompt: I wanted to talk about the technology we're looking for.

responses.text: Okay, I won't! {cheerily}
Yeah, but only if you've got bodies to fill the suits. We don't take on new members. We're all descendents from the original Brotherhood.
Something's going to have to change, or the empty suits are gonna be all that's left of us.

topics.prompt: Power armor and laser rifles are still effective.

responses.text: I think you're right. We're getting desperate. Hardly enough people to sustain ourselves as a chapter. They'll see the light, sooner or later.
But I get the feeling if I don't take matters into my own hands, the change won't come in time to make a difference.

topics.prompt: The Brotherhood is living in the past. Eventually they'll have to change.

responses.text: Wow, you sound like Elder McNamara. I {slight emph} know I should. Hell, it's what I signed up for when I chose to stay into adulthood.
I know there's something worth saving in there. But we're in decline. Our membership is... decimated. There's got to be something we can do.

topics.prompt: If it's worked for this long, there must be something redeemable about their beliefs. Have faith.

responses.text: I know the odds aren't good, but I've gotta try. I can't lose them.

topics.prompt: None of that is going to change. It's part of the Brotherhood's identity.

responses.text: I don't know. I'm still thinking about what kind of role we could take on that would give us the best chance of survival.
But I think things are starting to come together.

topics.prompt: Why don't you do something about it?

responses.text: Sure, but how long before the NCR or Caesar's Legion track us down and take it by force anyway?
But if we recruited Knights from outside the group, maybe we could actually defend it.

topics.prompt: The Brotherhood has to isolate itself. Its knowledge is dangerous.

responses.text: Yeah. I've got the rest of my life to help them out. I can spare a little while to see things through with you.
{Smiling} Sure. I want to establish a connection with the Followers first, but as far as I know, drifting is part of the job description.

topics.prompt: Are you still going to travel with me?

responses.text: No, I think it is. I have to be resolved about this. If I waver, it'll just make things harder.
They need me and I'm not going to abandon them.

topics.prompt: It's not too late to change your mind.

responses.text: I think so. Two things the Brotherhood has a lot of - hardheads and lasers. Wouldn't be the first time a disagreement ended like this.
Plus... we killed all the witnesses.

topics.prompt: Will they take you back after you killed these people?

responses.text: {Somber} Good idea.
I think that'd be best. There's a Followers outpost up near one of my old scavenging grounds. Used to do some trading with a doctor there.
If I work out of there, I'll still be able to keep tabs on Hidden Valley if I needed to. I know that route like the back of my hand.
If it's all right, I'd like to head that way. Meet some people, see if I can be of any use.

topics.prompt: Come on. Let's get out of here.

responses.text: Yeah. I think if I stayed I'd end up causing trouble. Sometimes I just can't help myself.
This way is better for me and for them.

topics.prompt: You're sure you're okay leaving them behind?

responses.text: Well, I shouldn't have come within a mile of here. I know that. {Beat} These poor people.
Seems like either way, there's not much I can do to help anyone.
I think maybe it's safer if I don't try.

topics.prompt: Maybe you should've stayed at Hidden Valley.

responses.text: {Not taking comfort} No... I don't, do I? If I did, none of this would've happened.
I should've left a long time ago. Cut my losses before it came to this.
I never stood a chance.

topics.prompt: You don't control the people who did this.

responses.text: {Sad, peeved} Isn't that what I just said? I know I'm responsible.
I was just trying to put it all behind me. Find someplace where what I do would actually have some influence.
I should've expected this, though. Different story, same ending.

topics.prompt: These people are dead because you were careless and selfish.

responses.text: No. Not a chance in hell. I'm not risking this happening again.
I'm gonna have to keep to myself. Better that way. For everyone.
I'll still finish what I started with you, though. If you're not afraid, that is. I'll just try not to get too caught up in it all.

topics.prompt: You can just join the Followers somewhere else.

responses.text: Okay, so take the Brotherhood. Replace their knowledge of superweapons with half as much knowledge of medicine and farming.
Sprinkle in a little compassion for people outside their group and healthy disrespect for authority, and voila. Followers.
I never really considered joining before. But now that I think about it, it really sounds like it could be a good fit, doesn't it?

topics.prompt: Who are the Followers of the Apocalypse?

responses.text: I want... a dress.
I would say he was my tutor, but that doesn't cover it.
After my parents passed, he looked after me. The whole Brotherhood brought me up, really, but he made sure of it.
I never had a grandfather - not that I knew, anyway - but Elijah was in some ways what I'd imagine a grandfather to be.

topics.prompt: Who was this Father Elijah to you?

responses.text: Just my parents, but they haven't been around for a long time. Dad was a Paladin, Mom was a Scribe.
They died in the same battle trying to hold off the NCR from... something. I don't remember what it was. Guess it seemed important at the time.

topics.prompt: Do you have any other family in the Brotherhood?

responses.text: If you take trying to keep me as far away from Hidden Valley as possible because I ask too many difficult questions as a sign of respect, {"absolutely"} oh yeah.
That's not to say I don't get along with them. I just think they don't know what to do with me sometimes.

topics.prompt: Are you well respected among other members of the Brotherhood?

responses.text: Yeah! A good one. Something elegant and classy, you know? But still stylish.
Something that's eye-catching and sexy, but also says "don't fuck with me."
I keep hoping I'll come across some Old World designer gown when I'm scavenging, but it never happens. Maybe I should move back to California.
Can I make it up?
Like what?

topics.prompt: Tell me something else about you.

responses.text: Hey, you try getting a date wearing Scribe robes. Might as well be wearing sweatpants.
I just like 'em, you know? They make you feel like a woman. Those ladies before the War, they knew what they were doing.

topics.prompt: That's your goal? You want a nice dress?

responses.text: I don't know. Last time anyone saw him was in the battle at HELIOS One. I wasn't there.
He gave orders to hold the plant until it could be reactivated. But he ran out of time. The NCR overran it. Everyone thought he was dead.
But I got a note from him at a comm station. That's... how he liked to talk, even to me. He wasn't good at face-to-face.
Yeah. I miss him.
Elijah could look at an old device and immediately understand what made it work. And he could see its potential. Where it fit with other technology.
It's not something you can teach, but he tried with me. {Shrugging} Some of it stuck.
But that's what he taught me. You asked what I {emph} learned from him.

topics.prompt: What did you learn from him?

responses.text: {Elongate the 'o'} Okay.
I learned what I don't want to become.
In the end, there was just him and his vision. Nothing and no one else.

topics.prompt: How is that different? What did you learn from him?

responses.text: It was... strange. Even for Father Elijah. He's always been unstable, but this was... something else.
I don't want to say delusional, but I don't know what else to call it. The only thing familiar about it was the signature.
He said the Brotherhood was doomed, but that he'd return, save us. But the {emph} way he said it... I don't know...
{Skeptical, but ominous} Said he'd return with one of the greatest treasures of the Old World, make the Mojave like it was meant to be... wipe the slate clean.

It was by his request, actually. He cleared it with the other Elders. {To herself} Somehow. {Veronica says the last part to herself b/c she doesn't understand how Elijah was able to convince the Elders (he tricked them).}
They sent him to look into the Dam. There was a time when I'd have begged to follow. Watch him at work.

topics.prompt: Did you follow him from California?

responses.text: {Emph} He did. For years, he fought with the Council. Taught me to question our direction. Meanwhile he'd become more out-of-touch than all of them.
On our way East he demanded we stop at HELIOS One to examine it. While we were there, we received word that the NCR had taken the Dam.
He was furious. Called it "children playing with a bomb." But he was mad because we'd lost its power. What we'd use it for... he didn't even care.
{Sadly} Yeah, I did. I couldn't help him.
{Slight frustration} He just didn't listen. And the idea that people talked {emp} back to him...
{Sighs} If he could have made the Brotherhood act like machines, ordering them around with a push of a button, he would have.

topics.prompt: Ever try to talk sense into him?

responses.text: They're cautious. When they discover something, they respect it, learn its limits, consider how to preserve it. Used to drive Father Elijah crazy.
He liked to learn limits, too, but only so he could push them.
That's not to excuse the other Elders, though. They all covet technology for its own sake. Some are just more fanatical than others.

topics.prompt: How is that different from how any other Elder would've reacted?

responses.text: It was the Dam, really. We'd heard rumors it was working. Figured we could claim it, put it to use.
{Putting it delicately} And... it may also have been partly that our Elder at the time had worn out his welcome.
Didn't end up mattering. We got sidetracked at HELIOS One and the NCR took the Dam in the meantime. We're still after it, though. In theory.

topics.prompt: Why is the Brotherhood interested in Nevada?

responses.text: {Playful} Ever been nosy?
{Sincere} I was, once. We were pretty young, but I like to think it was love.
She left the Brotherhood. Wanted to put some distance between herself and her parents.
Since our membership isn't open to outsiders, some members think that obligates all of us to procreate.
You can guess which camp her parents belonged to.
No. Couldn't bring myself to leave everyone else behind. Couldn't convince her to stay, either.
I'd hoped love would be enough to influence her decision, but it wasn't. We were both too stubborn.
I don't know where she is now, but I'm sure she's moved on. I still think about her, though. Once in a while.
Ooo. Got any juicy gossip?
{Pleasant} Sure.

topics.prompt: I want to discuss other things.

responses.text: All right, put 'em up. Let's see what you got.
You sure? Some other time, then.
Yeah. I've been taking things apart and putting them back together since before I said my first word.
You want to build something, talk to me, and we can do it right there on the spot. Workbenches are for novices.
Who knows, I might even be able to show you a Brotherhood trick or two.
Nowhere specific. I just know there are a lot of groups who're actually doing well for themselves out here.
I want to understand how and why. See them at work.

topics.prompt: Is there someplace you wanted me to take you?

responses.text: Don't take too long, all right?
Thanks. Wasn't wild about sticking around here on my own.

topics.prompt: I changed my mind. I'm not going inside, either.

responses.text: You killed him? {Beat} But...

topics.prompt: I had to kill him before he hurt others.

responses.text: Trapped him? Where?

topics.prompt: He's trapped, no chance of him escaping.

responses.text: {Default Choke Node} ...it doesn't matter. He died when we all retreated to Hidden Valley. I didn't expect to see him again, no one did.
Where did you get this?

topics.prompt: There's something I wanted to pass along.

responses.text: {Given a farewell message} All right, I'll listen to it.

topics.prompt: It's a message. The news is up to you.

responses.text: {Confused, a little disoriented} The parts I understood? Didn't matter. Past all the garbage, all it amounted to was goodbye.
{Watched a goodbye message, slightly choked up} That was... that was hard to watch.
{Irritated} Fine. I guess it doesn't matter anyway, keep it. I won't ask again.

topics.prompt: Yes. It was entrusted to me, not you.

responses.text: {Irritated} Fine. I guess it doesn't matter anyway, keep it. I won't ask again.

topics.prompt: Unlock it, give it back, then shut up.

responses.text: {Narration} At odds with leadership over the Brotherhood's future, Veronica looked to the Mojave Wasteland for an answer both she and they could live with.
{Narration} But the answer would never come, and the dangers of the world that had left the Brotherhood of Steel behind would eventually claim her life.
{Narration} Hoping to lead the Mojave Brotherhood down a new path, Veronica sought to learn from the thriving cultures of the desert.
{Narration} Absent a firm solution, Veronica's expression of frustration with Brotherhood leadership would lead to her banishment.
{Narration} She ended her days a wandering tinker.
{Narration} Despite her departure from the group, the Brotherhood's peace treaty with NCR came as some relief to Veronica.
{Narration} Though she remained friendly with surface patrols, she was never again permitted to enter the bunker she once called home.
{Narration} Fearing for the safety of anyone she associated with, she continued her solitary life as a scavenger.
{Narration} But reports would emerge from Mojave scientists and social workers of old equipment miraculously repaired and research notes mysteriously completed.
{Narration} Though she'd seen the writing on the wall, the destruction of the Mojave Brotherhood came far more suddenly than Veronica had expected.
{Narration} The news devastated her. Despite her best efforts to leave her past behind, she found herself compelled to make one final journey to Hidden Valley.
{Narration} There, she paid her last respects to the only family she had ever known.
{Narration} The Brotherhood's open aggression along the New Vegas highways troubled Veronica greatly.
{Narration} Nevertheless, it removed all doubt from her mind that in leaving them she had made the right choice.
{Narration} Eventually she would take to the road, less in hopes of finding a new home than of leaving memories of the old one behind her.
{Narration} The peace with NCR served to ease Veronica's worries about the Brotherhood's immediate future.
{Narration} Still, a distance had arisen between her and her fellow members that would never be bridged.
{Narration} She began secluding herself in crumbling libraries of the Old World, learning of promising technologies she knew the Brotherhood would never adopt.
{Narration} The death of the Mojave Brotherhood came much too soon for Veronica, and in their absence, she felt truly lost.
{Narration} Yet in its wake, she took small comfort in her decision to remain by their side through their few remaining days.
{Narration} Veronica put her moral sensibilities aside and supported the Brotherhood's new campaign of aggression as best she could.
Yet deep down, she understood that it meant their end would surely be soon to follow.
